The $563.49 reference close is the pre-earnings close. If the stock gaps up 5% on the beat, the 10% stop at $507.14 actually sits about 14% below the fill. If it gaps down, part of the stop distance is gone before we own it. (3) The beat is thin. Sales were $892.0M vs $885.7M, about +0.7%, and adj. EPS $5.11 vs $5.02, about +1.8%. The news inputs contain nothing on guidance: the transcript item is just a stub. So calling the beat 'clean' and saying 'the earnings risk is behind it' goes beyond the data, and the second invalidation leg ('guidance cut') is something nobody has checked yet. (4) The fundamentals-analyst notes it failed leverage_not_up, which the thesis omits, and the FY2025 fundamentals predate this quarter. Its closest peer, MCO (also labelled Industrials), reports tomorrow with high event risk, so a read-across move is possible within a day. rejected.why: The Skeptic's case is the strongest in the set and I agree. RRC was not ranked by the Fundamentals Analyst and has an F-score of 7 with leverage up and margin not improved. Its 10-28 earnings estimate sits inside the window and the 'already reported' argument rests only on an unread 8-K. It would be entering after a roughly 9% sector run driven by oil and Hormuz headlines. As the Implicator notes, the negative beta is not a reliable hedge, and the XLE 200-day invalidation is far too distant to protect anything. It would also be a second bet on the same Iran-deal headline as BTC. I would reconsider once the 8-K is confirmed or earnings have passed.
